origin.description: Locate the last non-overlapping regular-expression match in each string.
origin.usage: stri_locate_last_regex(str, pattern, capture_groups = FALSE, get_length = FALSE, ..., opts_regex = NULL)

arguments.name: str
arguments.text: Character vector of strings to search.

arguments.name: pattern
arguments.text: Character vector of regular expressions. An empty pattern is not supported.

arguments.name: capture_groups
arguments.text: If TRUE, attach one matrix per capture group.

arguments.name: get_length
arguments.text: If TRUE, the second column is the match length.

arguments.name: opts_regex
arguments.text: A list of regex settings, or NULL for the defaults.

origin.details: A missing string or pattern, or an empty pattern, yields a missing result, and an empty pattern warns. An empty string is searched. The inputs are recycled to the longer length. Positions are 1-based inclusive code points. A zero-length match has end equal to start minus 1. get_length reports length instead of end, and a miss is -1, -1. A missing string stays NA, NA. capture_groups attaches one matrix per parenthesized group. Group names are kept when the pattern is a single pattern. opts_regex holds only the settings that were supplied. Named arguments are merged into that dict and passed through stri_opts_regex. A repeated name is an error. An unknown name in a bare dict warns and is ignored. case_insensitive, comments, dotall (also dot_all), literal, multiline (also multi_line), unix_lines, and uword are ICU flags. error_on_unknown_escapes rejects an unknown backslash. time_limit and stack_limit are applied only when they are positive. The search runs from the start and skips overlaps. The result is one matrix, with one row per string.
origin.value: A two-column matrix with one row per string.
